messages:
alex: Heads-up — seeing intermittent allow on reads to /customer-artifacts in staging. ~2% of requests returning 200 where our policy should deny.
alex: sample log: `iam_eval: user=svc-analytics role=analytics, resource=customer-artifacts/12345, decision=ALLOW, reason=condition_true`
alex: cc @maria @jon — this looks like a policy eval problem after last night
maria: on it. can you paste the policy blob you saw?
jon: if this is related to the rbac-refactor PR I merged last night (PR #4567) i'll start rollback but want quick confirmation
alex: policy snippet from the live evaluator: ```{"effect":"ALLOW","actions":["read"],"resource":"customer-artifacts/*","condition":"resource.tags.env == 'prod' || user.attr.service_role == 'analytics'"}```
alex: the OR there should be AND — that would let analytics svc read prod artifacts unintentionally
maria: yikes. that OR got introduced in the condition-simplifier in the refactor. looks like short-circuiting broke boolean normalization
security-oncall: Emergency mitigations: 1) apply a deny-override to customer-artifacts/* immediately, 2) rotate creds for any svc accounts with analytics role, 3) enable verbose audit logs for artifact reads. Do we have a quick command?
jon: rolling back PR now, but we should do the deny-override first so rollback isn't racing with traffic
security-oncall: run: `infractl iam put-policy --name deny_customer_artifacts_temp --policy 'deny read resource:customer-artifacts/* if true' --scope global --ttl 1h`
sre-bot: policy deny_customer_artifacts_temp applied by infractl-user at 2026-03-20T14:08:02Z :white_check_mark:
maria: started rotating svc accounts: svc-analytics-1, svc-analytics-2. Creating short-lived tokens and rebind to constrained role. ETA ~20m
jon: PR #4567 reverted (link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4567) — will open follow-up to add unit tests for boolean normalization and an integration eval for condition combos
alex: quick check on KMS/KCV — does this incident require rekey? reads only, keys look untouched. We should still log KMS access to be safe
security-oncall: agree no rekey needed, but add KMS audit check to the postmortem. I'll create an incident and timeline doc. Action items: (A) deny-override applied, (B) creds rotated, (C) PR reverted, (D) tests added + integration eval, (E) KMS audit, (F) run a small canary in staging for 2 hours then remove ttl on deny and replace with correct policy
maria: can we also add an alert to detect condition expressions containing `||` on policy review? might catch similar regressions
jon: yes, adding a linter rule and a policy unit-test template. I'll pair with @maria tomorrow
alex: thanks all. monitoring looks good so far, no customer data confirmed leaked. will follow up in the incident doc. :thumbsup:
security-oncall: assigning postmortem owner: maria. please include root cause, timeline, and recommended guardrails.
maria: will take it. starting the write-up now and will tag everyone for review.
